title: US Energy Dept orders PJM to use data-centre and other backup generators as a last resort, 13-16 Oct
description: Energy Secretary Chris Wright issued an emergency order for the PJM grid (mid-Atlantic) ahead of high demand and planned generator outages. It authorises PJM to direct backup generation to run as a last resort before or during an Energy Emergency Alert 3, and DOE says over 35 GW of unused backup generation exists nationwide.
quote: authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3.
analysis: A major grid operator is now allowed to call on customer-owned backup gensets, which makes remote start, paralleling and emissions-compliant run hours part of what large buyers will ask for in standby packages. Action: brief the data-centre sales team on Cummins grid-support / demand-response genset controls so Gulf hyperscaler bids can answer the same question.

title: Cuba grid collapse on 18 Sept leaves a maternity hospital briefly without backup power as microgrid and generator fail
description: Cuba's national grid suffered its eighth total collapse of 2026 on 18 September; the Fe del Valle Ramos maternity hospital in Manzanillo lost power when its microgrid failed at the same time as its generator. The hospital said the gap was brief and reported no medical complications.
quote: a failure in this microgrid coincided with a malfunction in the institution’s generator, leaving the hospital without backup power for what the management described as a brief period.
analysis: The page shows a hospital standby chain failing in sequence (microgrid, then generator), which is the failure that healthcare buyers' maintenance and testing contracts are meant to prevent. For Cummins Arabia it is a reference case, not a Gulf demand signal. Action: use it as a talking point for hospital service-agreement renewals (load-bank testing, remote monitoring).

title: Malaysia asks telcos to cut diesel genset reliance at about 60,000 towers
description: On 28 September Malaysia's Communications Minister told telecom operators to reassess their dependence on diesel gensets at some 60,000 towers, especially in rural areas, and to move towards renewables under the National Energy Transition Roadmap. The government is convening partners to build a cooperation framework and possible incentives.
quote: The government has called on telecommunications companies to reassess their reliance on diesel generator sets (gensets) to operate some 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide, particularly in rural areas.
analysis: Telecom is a long-tail genset market and a government is now pushing it towards solar-battery hybrids, which is the direction GCC telcos could also take for remote sites. The page is about Malaysia only and gives no Gulf data. Action: ask Cummins Arabia's telecom accounts whether any tower or remote-site hybrid pilots are planned and whether Cummins has a battery-hybrid offer ready.

title: Ivanhoe: hybrid solar-battery plant at Kamoa-Kakula cuts diesel generator use by about 40% in September
description: Ivanhoe Mines reported that the on-site hybrid solar facility with battery storage at Kamoa-Kakula (DRC) delivers 60 MW continuously over 24 hours and led to roughly a 40% fall in diesel generator consumption in September. The company plans to double the site's solar capacity within 18 months.
quote: Kamoa-Kakula’s on-site hybrid solar facility with battery storage led to a 40% decrease in diesel generator consumption of about 40% in September.
analysis: A large mine is showing that solar plus battery can take a big share of run hours from diesel gensets, which shrinks prime-power fuel and service revenue per site while keeping gensets as firm backup. Action: when quoting Gulf mining or remote-site power (for example in KSA), position gensets as the firming layer in hybrid designs and price the service contract on reduced run hours.

title: Hurricane Isaias leaves up to 950,000 US Gulf Coast customers without power; 160,000 still out on 12 Oct
description: Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm on the night of 9 October; peak outages were about 950,000 per the Edison Electric Institute and about 160,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were still without power on 12 October. Utilities said grid modernisation sped up restoration.
analysis: Multi-day storm outages are the standard trigger for emergency generator and rental demand in the US, but the page does not cover generator sales and has no Gulf link. It matters to Cummins Arabia mainly as a signal that global rental and standby inventories may be drawn down. Action: check with Cummins rental and parts planning whether US storm demand is tightening rental-genset or parts supply for Gulf orders.

title: Bangkok halts new data-centre approvals and new licences for emergency diesel fuel storage
description: On 2 September the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and Thailand's Energy Ministry suspended approvals for new data centres in the capital and stopped issuing new licences for diesel storage that feeds emergency backup generators. The pause stays until a Data Centre Board sets criteria on water, electricity and environmental impact; the existing storage ceiling is 500,000 litres.
quote: Both the Ministry of Energy and the BMA confirmed that all new licences for emergency fuel storage for data centres have already been suspended.
analysis: Cities are starting to regulate the on-site diesel stock that sits behind data-centre standby gensets, not just the engines, which can cap run time or force gas or battery alternatives. The page covers Bangkok only; no GCC authority is mentioned. Action: confirm fuel-storage limits in current UAE and KSA data-centre permit conditions so Cummins Arabia bids size day-tanks and run-time correctly.

title: US EPA finalises partial repeal of 2024 carbon standards for power plants, including CCS rules for new base-load turbines
description: On 17 September EPA published a final rule repealing most of the 2024 greenhouse-gas standards for fossil-fuel power plants, including the carbon-capture-based Phase 2 standards for new base-load stationary combustion turbines. A concurrent supplemental proposal asks for comment on rescinding all GHG requirements for these units.
quote: and the 2024 CCS-based standards for new base load stationary combustion turbines
analysis: Lighter US carbon rules make on-site gas generation for data centres easier to permit, which supports gas genset and turbine demand in the US more than diesel standby. The rule is US-only and does not change Gulf requirements. Action: no Gulf action; keep as context when customers compare US gas-prime-power designs for hyperscale sites.

title: POWER conference: federal approach lets data centres meet grid-emergency limits by switching to backup generation
description: At Data Center POWER eXchange 2026 in Washington, former White House energy adviser Peter Lake urged developers to accept flexible interconnection, cutting grid withdrawals during emergencies in return for faster connection. He said the federal requirement does not prescribe how, and options include running backup generation, pausing workloads or shifting them between sites.
quote: A facility could switch to backup generation, pause suitable computing workloads, or shift workloads among a network of data centers
analysis: Flexible-connection rules give on-site gensets a second job (grid-emergency capacity) alongside standby, which supports larger and better-controlled genset plants at data centres. The statement is a US policy view from one speaker, not a Gulf rule. Action: ask Gulf utilities (SEC, DEWA, EWEC) whether similar flexible-connection terms are planned, and prepare a genset-plus-controls offer for them.

title: Victoria (Australia) tells new data centres to supply their own renewable energy and storage
description: The Australian state of Victoria announced a regulatory framework on 22 September under which new data-centre operators must provide their own renewable supply and storage, match added demand with new generation, and cover connection costs and network upgrades. Enerdata's summary of the state statement is dated 23 September.
quote: data centre operators will first be required to provide their own renewable energy supply and storage
analysis: Rules that push data centres towards on-site renewables plus storage point to battery-plus-genset designs where gensets cover firm capacity and outages; the page does not mention gensets, so this is our reading. The rule is Australian and does not bind GCC projects. Action: ask hyperscale clients in KSA and UAE whether their global design standards are moving towards storage-led backup, and have a genset-with-battery option ready.

title: North America adds rigs for a third straight week: Baker Hughes count at 825, 603 in the US
description: Baker Hughes' count published on 9 October showed North America up 11 rigs week on week to 825, with the US up five to 603 (462 oil, 132 gas) and Canada up six to 222. Rigzone reported the third consecutive weekly increase.
quote: North America added 11 rigs week on week, according to Baker Hughes' latest North America rotary rig count, which was published on October 9.
analysis: More active rigs means more oilfield power demand (rig and site gensets, gas-fuelled sets, rental), but the page gives only North American drilling counts, not genset orders or Gulf activity. Treat it as a weak global signal. Action: use Cummins Arabia's own oil and gas customer pipeline, not this count, to size Gulf demand.

title: Data-centre developers are buying gas engines 'in record numbers' as gas-turbine slots run to 2032
description: POWER reports that US data-centre developers face gas-turbine delivery dates as late as 2032 and are hedging by buying gas engines, fuel cells, batteries and renewables, while Applied Digital ordered 1.2 GW of steam turbines fed by gas-fired boilers. The article cites Siemens Energy, Solar Turbines and Mitsubishi Power as reporting similar supply delays.
quote: They are also hedging their bets—purchasing gas engines, too, in record numbers as well as fuel cells, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and renewable energy.
analysis: Long turbine lead times push prime-power buyers towards reciprocating gas gensets, which is where Cummins competes with Caterpillar, Rolls-Royce mtu and Jenbacher, and the same shortage may lengthen engine and genset slots. The page is about US projects. Action: ask Cummins factory for current gas-genset slot dates and tell Gulf data-centre and industrial prospects early.

title: Aggreko US listing filing shows two data-centre contracts totalling 221 MW, about a tenth of its gas fleet
description: An Electron Economics review of Aggreko's 24 August F-1 says the prospectus discloses two recent contracts with an unnamed large US data-centre developer, 135 MW and 86 MW, totalling 221 MW. It puts Aggreko's gas generation at 2.1 GW and argues the fastest-growing contracts are long, competitively tendered ones.
quote: The prospectus also discloses two recent contracts with a large American data-center developer, which it does not name.
analysis: Power-rental firms are putting large gas fleets behind data-centre bridge power, a business that competes with owning gensets and that also buys engines from OEMs. This is a secondary newsletter review of the filing (the SEC filing itself was not opened) and covers US contracts only. Action: check how Aggreko's Gulf rental offer and pricing compare with Cummins Arabia's rental and bridge-power proposals.
